title: Get online, save data and spot a fake website

say: Get online, save data, and spot a fake website.
This is the video for module one of Internet Basics and Online Safety: getting online with your smartphone.
The internet is a huge network of cables, masts and servers. Think of it as the roads that join towns.

items: The internet is the network itself

say: The letters by your signal bars matter. E or 2G is very slow. 4G or LTE is good for video.

say: Here is an example from the course. Halima in Kaduna has a video call with her cooperative. Ten minutes before, her screen shows one bar and the letter E.
She knows E means very slow 2G, too slow for video.

panel.heading: Halima reads her icons before a call
left: One bar and the letter E

say: So she walks about 20 metres to the front of the compound. Now she sees three bars and 4G.
She turns off a weak Wi-Fi that keeps dropping, joins the call, and switches her own camera off to keep it steady.
Tip: if pages will not load, turn Airplane mode on for ten seconds, then off again.

panel.heading: Halima reads her icons before a call
left: One bar and the letter E

say: Now, data. Open Settings, search for Data Saver and turn it on.

panel.heading: Five settings that save data
items: Turn on Android Data Saver
WhatsApp: auto-download photos only, or nothing
WhatsApp: Use less data for calls
Video apps: choose Data saver or 360p
Play Store: update over Wi-Fi only

say: In WhatsApp, go to Storage and data, then Media auto-download. On mobile data, choose photos only or nothing.

say: For example, Ifeoma in Onitsha buys a 30-day bundle of about 6GB, but it keeps finishing in two weeks.

panel.heading: Ifeoma finds her data eaters
items: Bundle of about 6GB finished in 2 weeks
Data usage: Facebook about 2.5GB
Play Store updates about 1GB
Changed settings: lasts 30 days, 1GB left

say: She opens Mobile data usage in Settings. Facebook used about 2.5GB. She sets its videos to autoplay only on Wi-Fi.

panel.heading: Ifeoma finds her data eaters
items: Bundle of about 6GB finished in 2 weeks

Play Store updates about 1GB

say: Play Store updates used about 1GB, so she sets updates to Wi-Fi only, and turns on Data Saver.

say: The next month her bundle lasts the full 30 days, with about 1GB left over.
Buy bundles only through your network official code or app, or your bank app. Never pay a stranger promising cheap 50GB.

say: In the browser address bar you can type a web address or your search words. Type the important words, not a long sentence, and add your town when it matters.

panel.heading: Better searches, safer results
items: Type key words and a place: tailoring school Ibadan
Quotation marks keep a phrase together
site:nafdac.gov.ng shows one official site only
Skip results marked Sponsored for important tasks

say: Put quotation marks around an exact phrase to keep it together.

say: Type site, a colon, then an official address, to search only that site. Nigerian government sites usually end in dot gov dot n g.

say: Grace in Port Harcourt got an SMS telling her to update her BVN at a link. She did not tap it. She pressed and held it to read the address.

panel.heading: Read the web address before you trust it
items: Do not tap. Press and hold to see the address
Find the domain just before the first single slash
Check it is the organisation's real domain
Use the official app or a saved bookmark instead

say: The rule is: read the domain just before the first single slash. Scammers put a famous name at the front so it looks right at a glance.

panel.heading: Read the web address before you trust it
items: Do not tap. Press and hold to see the address

Use the official app or a saved bookmark instead

say: Her link ended in gtbank-ng-update dot com. That is not her bank's real domain. Watch for look-alike spelling, wrong endings and shortened links.

say: She opened her bank's official app, saw no warning, and called the number on the back of her ATM card to report it.

say: A common mistake is trusting HTTPS. Scam sites can have it too. It means the line is private, not that the site is honest.

panel.heading: Read the web address before you trust it
items: Do not tap. Press and hold to see the address

Check it is the organisation's real domain
Use the official app or a saved bookmark instead
panel.rule: HTTPS means a private line, not an honest website.

say: If a shopping or job site shows two or more of these signs, stop. Search its name with the word scam, and ask someone you trust.

panel.heading: Stop if you see two of these signs
items: Prices far below every other seller
Transfer to a personal account only
No address, only a WhatsApp number
A countdown timer rushing you
A fee before you are hired

say: To remember. The internet is the network, and the Web is the pages. Video eats the most data, so turn on Data Saver.
Buy bundles only through official channels. Read the domain before the first single slash. And for money, type the address or use the official app.
